scope: Selected measurement definitions and evidence from all 19 core studies; not an exhaustive inventory of every logged statistic.

records.title: On the Rollout-Training Mismatch in Modern RL Systems
records.measure: Cross-engine KL is plotted alongside accuracy; TIS uses the learner-to-behavior sampled-action ratio.
records.comparison: The formulation compares FSDP and vLLM at the old parameter snapshot.
records.interpretation_limit: The figure caption does not specify KL direction, vocabulary coverage, or the numerical reduction. Do not reconstruct these from the TIS formula.

records.title: Jet-RL: Enabling On-Policy FP8 Reinforcement Learning with Unified Training and Rollout Precision Flow
records.measure: Learning curves compare BF16 training with FP8 rollout across context lengths and task difficulty.
records.comparison: BF16 and mixed-precision training runs; rollout length and initial model capability are varied.
records.interpretation_limit: These experiments establish a learning discrepancy, not a common scalar TIM distance. The reference-policy KL loss is a different quantity.

records.title: FP8-RL: A Practical and Stable Low-Precision Stack for LLM Reinforcement Learning
records.measure: Mismatch KL is defined as D_KL(pi_FP8 || pi_train). Scaling and KV/attention ablations track it with learning curves.
records.comparison: Rollout versus training policies in the stated precision configuration.
records.interpretation_limit: The direction is explicit; the metrics paragraph does not fully specify the estimator, vocabulary coverage, or reduction. Do not equate it with full-vocabulary KL by default.

records.title: QuRL: Low-Precision Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Reasoning
records.measure: Behavior-to-proximal KL, E_behav[log(pi_behav/pi_prox)], and the maximum proximal-to-behavior ratio.
records.comparison: Quantized behavior policy against the proximal training policy used for correction.
records.interpretation_limit: KL and the maximum ratio describe different aspects of mismatch. The maximum depends on token population and batch size; this KL is not reference regularization.

records.title: QaRL: Rollout-Aligned Quantization-Aware RL for Fast and Stable Training under Training--Inference Mismatch
records.measure: Token-level distributions of the proximal ratio and mismatch weight; response-level geometric-mean ratios drive TBPO.
records.comparison: Current/old learner probabilities are separated from old learner/sampler probabilities.
records.interpretation_limit: The proximal and mismatch ratios have different denominators. Geometric-mean response ratios are not complete-response likelihood ratios.

records.title: Let the Batch Decide, On- or Off-Policy: Effective Sample Size for RL Post-Training
records.measure: Normalized ESS = mean(rho)^2 / mean(rho^2), formed from all-reduced ratio sums, squared sums, and valid-token counts.
records.comparison: Current learner/recorded behavior ratios across valid response tokens in the batch.
records.interpretation_limit: This includes parameter lag as well as execution differences. Uniform weights yield high empirical ESS even when their common value is not one.

records.title: AIS: Adaptive Importance Sampling for Quantized RL
records.measure: Mean absolute sampled-token log gap; ESS of truncated weights; standard-deviation amplification std(A*w_bar)/(std(A)+epsilon).
records.comparison: Current training and rollout probabilities on the mini-batch; reliability uses capped weights.
records.interpretation_limit: The gap controls correction necessity; capped-weight ESS controls reliability. Its value is not directly comparable with raw-ratio ESS in P3O.

records.title: Rethinking the Divergence Regularization in LLM RL
records.measure: Binary-TV probability shift defines the constraint geometry; accuracy, entropy, and response length characterize update outcomes.
records.comparison: Sampled-action probabilities of the current policy and the behavior anchor in the objective.
records.interpretation_limit: A constraint variable is not necessarily a separately logged TIM metric. Binary-TV on one sampled action is not full-vocabulary total variation.

records.title: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning
records.measure: Mismatch-K3 = mean(exp(d)-d-1), d=log(pi_train)-log(mu), on rollout tokens; post-synchronization inference-gap proxy and rollback rate.
records.comparison: Rollout-token learner/sampler comparison; candidate policy additionally examined after synchronization.
records.interpretation_limit: K3 estimates D_KL(mu || pi) under normalization/support assumptions. The inference-gap proxy and rollback rate measure update acceptance, not a policy distance.

records.title: QUADS: Stabilizing NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning for MoE via QUantization-error Alignment across Dual Sides
records.measure: Per-step maximum norm of train–inference log-probability differences; layer-wise MoE activation/output L2 discrepancies.
records.comparison: Paired training/inference execution under weight and activation ablations.
records.interpretation_limit: A maximum gap depends on the measured population. Layer-wise L2 also depends on tensor shape, scale, and measurement location.

records.title: ACRL: Adaptive Control of Training-Inference Discrepancy for Stable Reinforcement Learning
records.measure: Absolute sampled-action probability difference |pi-mu|; within-response means are averaged over a response group and compared with an initial/baseline reference X.
records.comparison: Training and inference probabilities at the old parameter snapshot; Y/X controls reweighting.
records.interpretation_limit: Absolute probability distance is not absolute log distance. Response/group weighting differs from one global token mean; the baseline normalizes a controller, not a universal tolerance.

records.title: HiFloat4 Format for End-To-End Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Large Language Models
records.measure: Activation/residual MSE and RMSE under 2:4 sparsification, together with precision ablations and learned performance.
records.comparison: A quantized tensor and its sparsified counterpart in the residual design; rollout/training precision arms in learning ablations.
records.interpretation_limit: The Figure 4 tensor errors are not paired learner–sampler probability distances. Precision ablations locate an error source but do not yield a common TIM scalar.

records.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
records.measure: Same-token cross-engine log-probability comparisons verify low-precision recipes. A separate agentic reference run reports a train–inference KL curve; true-on-policy mode reports zero sampled-token absolute difference.
records.comparison: Comparisons depend on the execution mode. True-on-policy re-scores completed sequences by prefill rather than retaining decode-kernel probabilities.
records.interpretation_limit: The different observations are not one universal metric or one low-precision experiment. Exact sampled-token scores do not imply equality over the entire vocabulary or remove parameter lag.

records.title: Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
records.measure: Conditional mean score and baseline drift motivate the method analytically; shared-objective learning curves test injected weight noise, quantization, and lag separately.
records.comparison: Correction rules share objective, advantages, sampler, and trainer; severe mismatch is used to separate methods within short runs.
records.interpretation_limit: The score expectation is a theoretical estimand, not automatically an empirically logged norm. Stress-test severity and failure time are not a calibrated distance scale.

records.title: Towards Full Pipeline FP8 Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
records.measure: Normalized MAE of FP8 probabilities and ratios versus BF16 shadow passes; lower/upper over-clipping classified by advantage sign and a BF16 branch counterfactual.
records.comparison: FP8 and BF16 shadow probabilities/ratios for the examined updates; negative-advantage lower-bound over-clipping requires r_BF16>1-epsilon but r_FP8<=1-epsilon.
records.interpretation_limit: Over-clipping is a counterfactual decision disagreement, not the ordinary clipping fraction. Ratio NMAE concerns update distortion and is not solely a fixed-snapshot learner–sampler distance.

records.title: QATFactory: A Versatile, Deployment-Aligned Framework for Quantization-aware Training and Distillation of LLMs
records.locator: Section 4.6, Figure 8 and Table 8; Sections 4.1–4.4 for QAD
records.measure: QARL reports loss, reward, completion length, post-export accuracy, and speed. The paper also reports teacher KL/top-1 agreement in its separate QAD experiments.
records.comparison: QARL versus BF16 RL and post-hoc quantization; QAD compares teacher/student fidelity on held-out corpora.
records.interpretation_limit: Teacher-student KL from QAD must not be presented as an online QARL learner–sampler mismatch measurement.

records.title: TRIAGE: Direction-Aware Mismatch Stabilization of Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
records.measure: Mean absolute sampled-token log gap, signed quantiles, advantage-conditioned amplifying/contracting masses, and segment-localization statistics; before/after replay audits directional motion.
records.comparison: Recorded generation log probabilities are fixed. The 30B characterization replays sampled MoE routes; 4B measures the ordinary gap. Marginal statistics include all valid completion tokens; gradient-bearing occupancy excludes zero advantage.
records.interpretation_limit: The paper explicitly does not compare raw 4B and routing-conditioned 30B magnitudes. Directional indicators are audited rather than assumed to predict every token update.

records.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models
records.locator: Section 3.1, Figure 4; Section 4.4, Figure 11; Appendix A
records.measure: Maximum/minimum log-probability differences; relative excess activation MSE (D_FP4-D_BF16)/D_BF16 across layers.
records.comparison: Paired train–rollout activation discrepancies under FP4 and BF16; online extrema accompany reward/entropy/test curves.
records.interpretation_limit: The excess MSE is a relative increase over BF16 train–rollout discrepancy, not quantized-versus-exact tensor reconstruction error. Extrema are not TRIAGE-style mean absolute gaps; exact reduction must be retained.

records.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization
records.measure: Mean full-vocabulary conditional D_KL(p_BF16 || q_quant) over identical BF16-generated prefixes, before temperature scaling or sampling truncation.
records.comparison: Same policy checkpoint, paired KV execution, fixed prefix set; response-cluster bootstrap intervals.
records.interpretation_limit: This isolates a raw conditional numerical discrepancy, not actual post-decoding behavior probabilities, visited-prefix shift, or the online current-learner/old-behavior gap.
